Kevin — thanks for the clear asks. High level plan attached (MAP-v1.xlsx) and a draft of the rerank eval template. Quick summary of recommended approach below so your infra can triage:

- Phase 0: Preflight (3 days) — schema validation, sample priming (2k queries), capacity forecast.
- Phase 1: Seed wave (1% traffic) — backfill low-priority namespaces first; continuous parity checks; monitor write QPS and latency.
- Phase 2: Staged reseed (10% -> 50% -> 100%) across three waves spaced 48-72 hours apart with manual gates.
- Hotspot mitigation: circuit-breaker on concurrent writes to a single shard (configurable to 50 writes/s per shard), per-client token bucket, and backpressure signals to client SDK.
- Vector DB: Pinecone is acceptable; if you need lower read tail latency under heavy qps we suggest a warmed caching tier in front of Pinecone (Redis TTL of top-K results) — added as an optional step.

I'll drop the rerank template (rerank-eval-template.csv) and the runbook spreadsheet into the Drive link and paste the acceptance criteria at the bottom of this thread.

Next steps: Marissa will coordinate the preflight checklist and set a start-date once you confirm maintenance windows.

—Jonas Weber
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

Kevin / Anya — adding operational details you'll want for the SRE review and cutover window proposals:

- Backfill throughput profile: default 500 documents/minute across all namespaces; ramp plan available in MAP-v1.xlsx.
- Lock-free index writes: we recommend idempotent writes (doc_id + upsert semantics) to avoid tombstone storms during retries.
- Stale-reads during reseed: we'll keep a read-fallback to the old index for 7 days to reduce regression risk.
- Smoke tests and acceptance: we run the rerank A/B for 48 hours on 5% traffic, monitor NDCG@10, CTR lift, and latency distribution (p95/p99). Thresholds in the CSV.

Can you confirm which namespace mapping you'll use for user-profiles vs. content? That affects shard allocation.

Attachments: rerank-eval-template.csv

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Transition plan: index reseed, hotspot mitigation, and A/B rerank tests

Anya — short answers from SRE/implementations:

- De-dup / ordered writes: prefer strictly-ordered upserts per doc_id using idempotency keys. Our backfill tool supports batched upserts with per-batch checkpoints; if a batch fails we rewind to previous checkpoint instead of reapplying the whole batch.
- Hotspot throttles: we advise a soft-shard-window limiter (configurable) and global concurrency cap for write workers. We can provide a Helm chart snippet that enforces these limits in your cluster.
- Rollback: we never delete the old index until the rerank A/B gates pass; the fallback path is automated in case of regressions.

I'll attach the Helm snippet to the Drive link and sync with your infra team next week.

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (drive), rerank-eval-template.csv (drive)

Ben Carter
